solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Showing variance about recording device has date wrong (13, two words)

indicators.note: one thing placed about another goes round it, wrapping it on both sides
letters that have gone wrong are out of their proper order and need rearranging

parts.note: the words taken letter for letter as fodder
a logger records readings automatically

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a data recorder has stamped the wrong date, putting it out of step.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Showing variance' sounds statistical, but it means in disagreement; the rearranged letters split into two parts on either side of the device.
explanation.definitionFit: People at loggerheads are in dispute, at variance with one another, so the idiom describes showing variance.

clue.text: Women (not men) entering hammer tossing game

indicators.note: something entering goes inside another word, which then surrounds it

parts.note: a tup is a ram, and also the striking head of a power hammer

indicators.note: 'not' tells us to take the following letters away from the word before

parts.note: taken as written
the letters to strip from the end of the previous word

explanation.surface: A game in which women, but no men, take part in hammer tossing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hammer tossing' looks like the athletics event, but 'tossing game' is the definition and the hammer is a ram's alternative name.
explanation.definitionFit: Two-up is an Australian gambling game in which players bet on how two coins spun into the air will land.

clue.text: Bit of gardening I like, rearing plant stiffener

indicators.note: in a down clue something rearing rises up, so the letters read from bottom to top
a bit of a phrase is a run of consecutive letters taken from inside it

parts.note: the run of letters spanning the end of gardening, I and the start of like

explanation.surface: A gardener admits fondness for some aspect of the work, perhaps staking plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Lignin is the woody polymer in plant cell walls that gives stems their rigidity, acting as a stiffener.

clue.text: Formation flyers, those on wings of gyrating energy

parts.note: the letters at each end of gyrating are both G, and the plural of the letter name gee is gees
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Birds flying in formation, those on the edges swirling energetically.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'wings' of the word gyrating are its first and last letters, two Gs, spelt out as GEES.
explanation.definitionFit: Wild geese famously migrate in V-shaped skeins, so they are birds that fly in formation.

clue.text: Plant mostly raised in dunes from the south

indicators.note: in a down clue reading from the south means reading upwards, from bottom to top
one word placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: areg is the plural of erg, a desert region of shifting sand dunes

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: raised as in reared, of animals or children

explanation.surface: A plant mostly grown among southern sand dunes.
explanation.walkthrough: An erg is a sandy desert of dunes; its unusual plural is areg.
explanation.definitionFit: A gerbera is a South African daisy-like flowering plant, popular as a cut flower.

clue.text: Timeless number among great lives possibly

indicators.note: something among other letters is placed in the midst of them
possibly signals the letters are one possible rearrangement of what is given

parts.note: the words taken letter for letter as fodder
N is the standard abbreviation for number

explanation.surface: A timeless song, perhaps, features in the lives of the great.
explanation.definitionFit: Something everlasting never ends, so it is timeless, unbounded by time: a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Church accepted distinction without hesitation for leader

indicators.note: a word that has accepted another has taken it in, so it surrounds it
without here means lacking, so the following letters are removed

parts.note: an honour is a mark of distinction
ur is a sound of hesitation, like er
CH is the usual abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: The church gave a figure an award, without hesitating, for leadership.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without hesitation' looks like an adverb for 'accepted', but the hesitation sound is the part removed.
explanation.definitionFit: A honcho, from Japanese for squad leader, is the boss or person in charge, as in head honcho.

clue.text: Nigerian submerged in drink if ever heading westwards

indicators.note: westwards is leftwards on a map, so the letters are read right to left
something submerged in a phrase lies under its surface, a run of letters within it

parts.note: the run of letters spanning the end of drink, if and the start of ever

explanation.surface: A Nigerian, if ever drowned in drink, would be heading west.
explanation.definitionFit: The Efik are a people of south-eastern Nigeria, so a member of that people is a Nigerian.

clue.text: Tree, one seen in African area

indicators.note: something seen in another word appears inside it

parts.note: Afr is the abbreviation for African
a, the indefinite article, means one
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A lone tree spotted in an African region.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a whole the clue also describes the answer, since it is a tree found across West Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Afara is a West African hardwood tree, also called limba, valued for its timber.

clue.text: Where you'll find dead shrivelled trees

definitions.text: Where you'll find dead shrivelled trees

indicators.note: something shrivelled is twisted out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for dead, as in genealogies
taken as written

explanation.surface: A question of where dried-out dead trees are to be found.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay: a parched landscape is just where withered dead trees stand.
explanation.definitionFit: A desert is an arid wasteland, the setting where little water means trees die and wither.

clue.text: Women in discarded dress making the old leer

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it

parts.note: tire is an obsolete word for attire, so dress that has been discarded from the language
W is the abbreviation for women

explanation.surface: Women in cast-off clothing attract an old man's leering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discarded' does not signal a deletion; it marks the word for dress as obsolete. 'The old' likewise marks the answer as archaic.
explanation.definitionFit: Twire is an archaic verb meaning to peer or glance slyly, close in sense to leering.

clue.text: Gambler worst off in the short run

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it
something off has gone bad or awry, so these letters are disordered

parts.note: the word taken letter for letter as fodder
taken as written
R is the short form of run, as on a cricket scorecard

explanation.surface: A gambler comes off worst in the short term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The short run' looks like a phrase meaning the near term, but it splits into THE and R.
explanation.definitionFit: A throwster is one who throws dice, so a dicer or gambler, in a rare sense of the word.

clue.text: One unpopular at opera in audience box?

indicators.note: what reaches an audience is what they hear, so the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: someone who keeps coughing during a performance annoys everyone around

explanation.surface: A spectator coughing in an opera box makes themselves unpopular.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Audience' fits the opera scene, but here it means listeners hearing the sound of a word.
explanation.definitionFit: A coffer is a strongbox or chest for valuables, so a box.

clue.text: Pet maybe making me very embarrassed! (9, two words)

parts.note: very embarrassed people go red in the face
the compiler refers to themselves, the setter of the puzzle

explanation.surface: Someone's pet does something that leaves its owner blushing.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords 'me' often means the setter; with RED in front it makes a dog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: The red setter, or Irish setter, is a gundog breed kept as a family pet, so an example of a pet.

clue.text: Mutton in the upper house George freely tucked into

indicators.note: something tucked into another is placed inside it

parts.note: HL stands for the House of Lords, the upper chamber of Parliament

indicators.note: letters arranged freely are not bound to their original order

parts.note: the name taken letter for letter as fodder

explanation.surface: Lunch in the House of Lords, with George freely tucking into the mutton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tucked into' suggests eating, which suits the mutton, but it signals insertion. Mutton here means the sheep itself, not the meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoggerel is a young sheep in its second year, and mutton can mean a sheep in old usage.

clue.text: List of Scotch concealed in bar (underneath)

indicators.note: something concealed in a phrase is tucked away among its consecutive letters

parts.note: the run of letters spanning the end of bar and the start of underneath

explanation.surface: A list of whiskies kept hidden under the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'List' is not a catalogue but the selvage or border strip of cloth; 'of Scotch' marks a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots a rund is the selvage of woven cloth, which in English is also called a list.

clue.text: Trained to admit blunder, looking very embarrassed!

indicators.note: a word that admits another lets it in, so it holds it inside

parts.note: bred as in brought up and schooled
rick is a short form of ricket, an old word for a blunder found in older Chambers editions

explanation.surface: Someone well brought up, made to own up to a gaffe, goes scarlet.
explanation.walkthrough: Rick for a blunder is rare enough that it appears only in older editions of Chambers.
explanation.definitionFit: Brick-red is a deep reddish colour, so describes a face flushed deep red from shame.

clue.text: Move on left in frozen state north of the border

definitions.text: frozen state north of the border

parts.note: jee is a variant of gee, a call to a horse to move on
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Being told to move left while frozen in a northern country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'North of the border' means in Scotland, marking a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeel is Scots for jelly or a congealed state, the condition of something set or frozen.

clue.text: Pant after a course overseer leading other ranks (7, two words)

indicators.note: one piece leading another goes in front of it in reading order

parts.note: taken as written
a chef oversees the courses of a meal
OR is the military abbreviation for other ranks, those not commissioned

explanation.surface: A runner pants behind a course marshal leading a group of soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course overseer' suggests a racecourse official, but the course is part of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: To pant after something is to long for it, which is what aching for it means.

clue.text: Garden implement without starter is trying

indicators.note: without its starter means lacking the first letter, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: shears are large garden scissors

explanation.surface: Using garden shears without a starter motor is hard work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trying' looks like an adjective meaning tiresome, but it is the legal sense: a judge trying a case hears it.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge hears a case when trying it in court, so hears equals is trying in the legal sense.

clue.text: Women engage in exchange about backing No. 1 with energy, creating early bloomer (13, two words)

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for women

indicators.note: a word placed about another goes round it

parts.note: to interact is to engage in an exchange with others

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: the abbreviation for number, taken as its letters
the Roman numeral for one
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Women chat around a top performer full of energy, coming out early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No.' turns round and is followed by the Roman I, and the pair go inside INTERACT before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Winter aconite is a small yellow flower that blooms in late winter, among the first of the year.

clue.text: Source of idolatry concentrated around one venerated?

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it begins, its first letter

parts.note: the opening letter of idolatry

indicators.note: one word around another surrounds it

parts.note: conc is the abbreviation for concentrated, as on a label
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Idol worship focused on someone treated as almost holy.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a loose definition: something iconic is held up like an icon, a revered image.
explanation.definitionFit: Iconic things are revered like icons, the holy images of the Orthodox church, hence venerated.

clue.text: Sharp-eyed youngster eyes missing quite ornamental tag

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so the next word's letters are taken away

parts.note: taken as written
quite! as an exclamation of agreement means yes
an aglet is the metal tag on a lace end, or an ornamental tag on a garment

explanation.surface: A keen-eyed youngster spots a missing decorative tag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quite' is the agreeing interjection, so EYES without YES leaves E.
explanation.definitionFit: An eaglet is a young eagle, and eagles are proverbial for sharp sight.

clue.text: Does it suggest whit Jock's enclosed?

parts.note: surface reading: a puzzle about whether one word hints at another
setter's reading: split the answer into IN, WIT and H, and it reads as an instruction to put H in WIT, which spells whit

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a Scottish word hints at a tiny amount hidden away.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer, split up, is wordplay whose result is whit. 'Jock's' marks a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Inwith is Scots for within, inside, describing what is enclosed by something.

clue.text: Part of opera featuring contralto in Indian army

indicators.note: a word featuring another includes it inside itself

parts.note: sena is a Hindi word for an army
C is the abbreviation for contralto

explanation.surface: An opera excerpt starring a contralto performed for an Indian regiment.
explanation.definitionFit: A scena is a dramatic solo scene in an opera, longer and freer than an aria.

clue.text: One man's taken up third space in bass section?

indicators.note: in a down clue something taken up is lifted from bottom to top, so read backwards

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
a man is a male

explanation.surface: One man has gone up to sing a note in the bass part.
explanation.walkthrough: The third space of the bass stave is the note E, named E la mi in the old hexachord system.
explanation.definitionFit: Elami is the old solmisation name for the note E, which sits on the third space of the bass stave.

clue.text: Special spring grass

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for special
to hop is to spring or jump

explanation.surface: A particular kind of springtime grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' is a verb here: British slang for informing on someone to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: To shop someone is British slang for betraying them to the police, the same as to grass on them.

clue.text: E.g. Lulu, some years after her forte, without No. 1?

indicators.note: the number one letter is the first, so without it the opening letter goes

parts.note: the singer Lulu is a pop star, so pop is her strong suit
an era is a span of years

explanation.surface: Lulu the singer's career, some years past her peak, without a number one hit.
explanation.walkthrough: Lulu is both Berg's opera and the Scottish pop singer; 'her' refers to the singer. POP loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Lulu is an unfinished opera by Alban Berg, so it is an example of an opera.

clue.text: A number trapped by hail in foreign capital

indicators.note: something trapped by another is enclosed within it

parts.note: to hail someone is to greet them, as with hi
taken as written
No is the abbreviation for number

explanation.surface: A group of people caught in a hailstorm abroad in a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hail' looks like the weather, but it is the greeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanoi is the capital city of Vietnam, a capital outside Britain.

clue.text: There's no free passage here — all to get hammered

indicators.note: something hammered is beaten out of shape, so the letters are reshaped

parts.note: the words taken letter for letter as fodder

explanation.surface: Nothing free here: everyone is going to get drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A tollgate is a barrier where travellers must pay a toll before going on, so passage is not free.

clue.text: League I'm in scoring first draw

indicators.note: scoring a letter out crosses it through, so the first letter is struck off

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for league
taken as written, without the apostrophe
taken as written

explanation.surface: A footballer's boast: my team scored first and drew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoring' and 'draw' suggest a match, but scoring means crossing out and draw means depict.
explanation.definitionFit: To limn is to depict or paint, especially in outline, the artistic sense of to draw.

clue.text: Squash mug

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to crush, as with a fly
second meaning: to study hard, as in mug up; a variant of swot

explanation.walkthrough: The pairing suggests a drink and a cup; both words are verbs, crush and cram.
explanation.definitionFit: To swat is to crush with a blow, and, as a variant spelling of swot, to study hard or mug up.

clue.text: Bit of liver I set before cat? It's on my palm

indicators.note: set before means placed ahead of the next piece in reading order
a small bit of a word is one letter, here its first

parts.note: the opening letter of liver
taken as written
a feline is a member of the cat family

explanation.surface: A palm reader's patter: put some liver out for the cat.
explanation.definitionFit: In palmistry the life line is a crease on the palm said to show length of life.

clue.text: With borders all round, less sunny having switched ends

indicators.note: switching ends swaps the first and last letters with each other

parts.note: a dimmer day has less sunshine

explanation.surface: A frame described as less bright once its edges were swapped.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rimmed has a rim, an edge or border, running around it.

clue.text: Propeller beginning to turn in moving ro-ro

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it
letters that are moving shift out of their order

parts.note: the letters of ro-ro, short for roll-on roll-off ferry

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the opening letter of turn

explanation.surface: A ferry's propeller starts turning as the roll-on roll-off ship moves.
explanation.walkthrough: A ro-ro is a roll-on roll-off ferry that vehicles drive straight on and off.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotor is a rotating blade assembly, such as the propeller on a helicopter.

clue.text: Showing results of body scan? Charting pics I become troubled

indicators.note: something troubled is disturbed and unsettled, so the letters are stirred up

parts.note: the words taken letter for letter as fodder

explanation.surface: A patient frets while charting the pictures from a medical scan.
explanation.definitionFit: Scintigraphy is a diagnostic imaging technique using radioactive tracers to picture organs, so scintigraphic images show scan results.
